title: A count of endings, and what it leaves out (worked out on cardboard)
note: The authored thinking for one hall, in the first person, by the pass (Claude), for Palle's request of 2026-11-14 (see Russell_Paradox.json). 'at' is the floor's own frame in metres (x east, z south), 'yaw' in degrees. A sticker of kind 'quote' stands word for word in the hall text; every other kind is mine and may be wrong - the plates say where I am unsure.

hero.why: The fan is what the hall text is about: a branching diagram that counts its leaves, with CYCLE, ONE, OPEN and PRUNE.
hero.staging: The visitor arrived inside the particle spray, with the fan at the far north edge; the pass restaged the floor (94f96be64). The fan is straight ahead of the arrival with its four buttons toward the visitor, the spray on the west wing; north of the fan the tree taped on the floor.

plates.title: 1  A FEW CHOICES, MANY FUTURES
front: How quickly can a few choices become many possible futures? Faster than I can picture.
One continuation at each of four levels: one path. Two: sixteen. Three: eighty-one.
It grows by multiplication: every earlier choice can be followed by all the later ones.
The fan draws all eighty-one at once. On the floor behind it I can only walk one.
That difference is the rest of this cardboard.
back: 3 x 3 x 3 x 3 = 81; 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 = 16. I did the sums; the fan's readout and the floor's stand agree with them.

plates.title: 2  TWO ENDINGS SHARE A BEGINNING
front: Pick two endings. Walk back from each until the paths meet.
L R R L and L R R R part at the last fork. L R R L and R L L R part at START.
They are different outcomes, and most of some histories is the same history.
Shared beginnings are how the count stays honest: it is not sixteen unrelated things.
I had been thinking of futures as a list. They are a tree, and the trunk is the past.
back: walked: the lit path shows the shared part; the tape beyond the fork is where they separate.

plates.title: 3  EQUAL LEAF WEIGHTS
front: The fan's readout says: equal leaf weights. Every ending is given the same probability. Then H is the logarithm of the count.
Nats here, bits on the last floor. The unit changes the number, not which endings are counted.
The logarithm is why four forks of two add up: four times ln 2.
But 'equal' was assigned, not found. Nobody watched travellers.
A count of endings is an inventory. It is not yet a forecast.

plates.title: 4  COUNTED, AND AS WALKED
front: The stand gives the entropy twice. Counted: ln 16 = 2.77. As walked: from where travellers actually arrived.
Three walks. Two ended at the same place, one elsewhere: 0.64.
Sixteen endings were drawn. Two were used.
The hall: a strongly preferred branch could make the actual distribution much more concentrated. I preferred a branch near the stand.
To know what will happen I need the arrivals as well as the drawing.
back: 0.64 = -(2/3 ln 2/3 + 1/3 ln 1/3). three walks is a tiny sample; that was the last floor's point.

plates.title: 5  HOW MANY IS NOT WHICH
front: PRUNE A: four gates, eight endings. PRUNE B: four gates, eight endings.
The same count. The same entropy, 2.08. Not one ending in common.
The hall says it of the fan: twenty-seven tells us how many endings remain, not which ones. Here I could walk to the difference.
A cut made early takes everything after it: each gate here removes two endings; on the fan each removes three.
To compare two closures I need the paths, not the total.
back: the stand prints the closed paths by name (L L R, L R R ...) because the number would not tell them apart.

plates.title: 6  OPEN RETURNS THE ENDINGS, NOT THE ARRIVALS
front: Two beads hung at one ending. PRUNE A closed the gate in front of it. The beads were gone.
OPEN: the gate is gone, the ending is back, the tape is back. The rod is empty.
The stand: 3 arrivals hung behind gates when they closed. OPEN returns the endings, not the arrivals.
On the fan the same endings return at a touch, and the hall says that ease is part of the experiment's limit.
I made the button a little less easy. It still costs nothing to press.
back: what the beads stand for is thin: three walks by a test walker. I do not want them to carry more than that.

plates.title: 7  PROHIBITED, OR NEVER DRAWN
front: An amber gate marks an option that was there and was refused. I can walk up to it.
A third way at every fork was never drawn at all. There is nothing to walk up to.
A picture of the permitted future can hide how the permissions were chosen.
Counting its endings cannot recover what was left out before the counting began.
Sixteen, or eight, or eighty-one: each number already contains somebody's decision about what a branch is.
back: including mine. two ways at each fork, four forks: I chose that because it fits the floor.

plates.title: 8  YOU CANNOT YET ASK IT TO GROW OTHERWISE
front: Who drew the tree? Who can ask for another branch, or refuse the condition for reaching one?
The fan has four buttons, and the hall is exact about them: you can reopen it; you cannot yet ask it to grow otherwise.
On the floor I left room for one kind of asking. Stand still at a last fork and a third way is drawn, in pink, to an ending nobody specified. Seventeen.
Only at the last forks. Only one more. Only forward.
So the answer to the hall's question is still: I did. Now with a suggestion box.
back: the hall asks that what a model leaves out keep the capacity to challenge and change its terms. a third way at a last fork is a small part of that, and I should not call it more.

plates.title: 9  MORE ENDINGS IS NOT MORE WAYS TO LIVE
front: Keeping every branch open is not automatically care. The hall: a closure might protect a place in which a more vulnerable body can continue.
My gates cannot tell which kind they are. Amber for all of them.
The count goes down by the same amount whether a gate shuts someone out or keeps something safe.
So the number is on neither side. It has to be asked: closed by whom, for whom, and can it be answered?
More endings on a screen. More ways to live. I can count the first.
back: I do not know how to build the second as a floor. that is an open item, not a modesty.

threads.why: Many possible futures are not, by that count, more ways to live.
Eighty-one, sixteen: the count becomes an entropy only by weighing every ending alike.
Equal weights were assigned; the walked tally is what was found.
Arrivals hung where travellers went; then a gate closed in front of them.
Endings are not a list to be lengthened: they share beginnings.
Shared beginnings are why two prunings with one total are different things.
Which endings were closed can be named; what was never drawn cannot even be pointed at.
What was never drawn can only arrive by being asked for.
The logarithm turns the forks' multiplication into addition along the shared trunk.

visual_arguments.title: WHO DREW THE TREE?
visual_arguments.claim: A count of endings says neither which endings nor who arrives at them; a reopened route does not return what was lost when it closed; and what was never drawn can only arrive by being asked for.
visual_arguments.from_the_hall: 'Eighty-one drawn leaves do not tell you that a traveller is equally likely to arrive at each one.' ... 'Twenty-seven tells us how many endings remain, not which ones.' ... 'You can reopen it. You cannot yet ask it to grow otherwise.'
built_from: white tape from START through four forks of two to sixteen blue plates
a rod behind every ending, a bead for each arrival
eight amber gates, four standing at a time
a pink tape and plate at a last fork where a third way was asked for
a stand with the count, the entropy twice, the closed paths by name, and what was lost
three plates: PRUNE A, PRUNE B, OPEN
visual_arguments.what_stands: North of the fan a white tree taped on the floor, fanning out to a row of sixteen blue plates with thin rods behind them, and a dark stand beyond.
visual_arguments.what_you_do: Walk from START to an ending: the path lights and a bead is hung. Do it again. Press PRUNE A, then PRUNE B, then OPEN, and read the stand each time. Stand still at a last fork.
visual_arguments.what_it_shows: ln 16 as counted against what was walked; two prunings of eight with nothing in common; beads lost behind gates and not returned; and a seventeenth ending that was not in the first drawing.
visual_arguments.measured: tools/probes/drawn_tree_walk.gd, the tower's walker: ln 16 by the fan's own rule; three arrivals at two endings: 0.64 nats; PRUNE A: 8 endings, 4 gates, 2 beads lost, the gate holds a body; PRUNE B: 8 other endings, the same entropy; OPEN: 16 endings, no beads, 3 lost; a third way asked for: 17 (7 of 7). Not tried in a headset.

open: Plate 9: how to build 'more ways to live' as a floor, as against more endings, the pass does not know. The gates cannot tell a closure that shelters from one that shuts out.
Plate 8: asking is possible only at the last forks, only for one more ending, only forward. Who drew the tree is still the pass.
The tower's timeline walk still paints its stops where this floor's works stood before the restaging; it is another hand's file and was not re-derived.

threads.why: Many futures drawn at once; a traveller walks one.
Much of the history is identical: the trunk of the tree is the past.
The unit changes the number; either way it numbers an inventory.
Drawn leaves are not arrivals: sixteen were drawn and two were used.
How many, not which: two prunings of eight with no ending in common.
The total cannot stand in for what was removed; the paths have to be named.
Reopening returns the route; the rod where arrivals hung is empty.
What was never drawn leaves nothing to walk up to.
Who drew the tree: the pass did, and left a suggestion box.
The fan cannot yet be asked; the floor can, a little, in one place.
Open is not automatically care, and the count cannot tell a gate that shelters from one that shuts out.
More endings and more ways to live: only the first can be counted here.
